dedupe_keys.name: adaptive post earthquake restoration of electricity gas distribution systems with damage inspection and repair crew routing

description: This framework by Mingxuan Li, Wei Wei, Yin Xu, Chengeng Zhang and Shanshan Shi, accepted in the CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems (arXiv 2026), restores integrated electricity and gas distribution systems after an earthquake when damage is not fully known because monitoring and communication infrastructure are impaired. Coverage: restoration is formulated as a partially observable Markov decision process that captures damage revealed gradually by field inspection and the effect of crew actions; a belief tree search algorithm lets crews update inspection and repair actions as their beliefs change, using simulations of future trajectories, within one real-time decision framework. Case studies on two integrated systems show outage costs close to the ideal solution with full damage knowledge and more than 15% lower than stochastic programming and heuristic strategies. Format and access: an arXiv preprint. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated on the abstract page. Caveats: test systems, not a named utility; code is not mentioned. The formulation can drive emergency response and restoration sequencing for gas and power lifelines in resilience models. It relates to the IN-CORE interdependent network model and the Centerville gas recovery study in the catalogue.
